newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-LACKLUSTRE BRAZIL BEAT COLOMBA 1-0 IN COPA AMERICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LACKLUSTRE BRAZIL BEAT COLOMBA 1-0 IN COPA AMERICA.

text.p: Brazil beat Colombia 2-0 to record their third consecutive Copa America win Thursday despite being outplayed for long periods by their young, inexperienced opponents.
Brazil captain Dunga opened the scoring with a thundering, low shot from 30 metres in the 11th minute for his sixth goal in 73 full internationals.
Substitute striker Edmundo made sure Brazil finished top of group C when he added the second goal in the 67th minute from a rebound after a shot by Romario had struck defender Oscar Cordoba.
But much of the match was dominated by Colombia, who finished third in the group with three points and also qualified for the quarter-finals as one of the two best third-placed teams.
Colombia finished level on points and goal difference with Uruguay, who came third in group B but scored only two goals to Colombia's five.
The Colombians suffered a nervous last 20 minutes as another Brazil goal would have sent them home.
The result set up a fascinating quarter-final between Brazil and Paraguay on Sunday.
Mexico, who finished second in the group after drawing 1-1 with Costa Rica earlier Thursday, will face Ecuador on Sunday while Colombia travel to La Paz to face Bolivia Saturday.

Brazil's much-vaunted striking pair Ronaldo and Romario were superbly contained by Jorge Bermudez and Ivan Cordoba and the former was substituted on the hour to a chorus of jeers from the large Brazilian contingent in the crowd.
Veteran coach Mario Zagallo was jeered with every substitution by fans who chanted "stupid, stupid."

Despite his goal, Dunga, as in several recent matches, added little else to the game, spending most of his efforts initimidating opponents. He was taken off five minutes later after receiving a yellow card.
Zagallo's consolation, apart from the result, was that the Goncalves-Aldair partnership in the centre of the defence looked far more secure than other combinations he has tried recently.

"Efficiency in football is judged by victories," said Zagallo. "Some days you play well, other days badly but what counts is the victory. I prefer to play ugly football and win than attractive football and lose."

Colombia, like many other teams in the competition, had decided to rest their top players for the region's World Cup qualifiers. Brazil as world champions qualify automatcially for France next year and brought a full-strength squad to Bolivia.
The best of their new players were Neider Morrantes in midfield and Cordoba and Bermudez in defence.
However, they were unable to transform some often excellent midfield play into goals and Brazil goalkeeper Taffarel was only severely tested three times throughout the game.
Colombia's best effort was a long range drive by Wilmer Cabrera which Taffarel tipped over his crossbar.
Teams:
Brazil - 1-Taffarel, 2-Cafu (14-Ze Maria, 74), 13-Goncalves, 3-Aldair, 17-Ze Roberto, 5-Mauro Silva, 8-Dunga (18-Cesar Sampaio, 85), 10-Leonardo, 20-Denilson, 9-Ronaldo (21-Edmundo, 61), 11-Romario

Colombia - 12-Miguel Calero, 4-Jose Santa, 5-Jorge Bermudez, 2-Ivan Cordoba, 15-Mauricio Mosquera, 13-Wilmer Cabrera, 6-Wilmar Perez, 18-Victor Bonilla (17-Hamilton Ricard, 46), 22-Neider Morrantes (8-Andres Estrada, 70), 9-Victor Hugo Aristizabal, 20-Victor Pacheco.
